authorizing_record: guillermomolina/protos#725 (PERF014, direct Closure-call stabilization: a definition-keyed fastDirect second tier - ProtosClosureValue.definition() -> CanonicalClosure -> entered Context -> Context-owned RootCallTarget - added on top of the first-tier receiver-identity-keyed mechanism, preserving dynamic Closure semantic instance identity and executing the D013 `call` authoritative selection on every hit). The product's own structural validation (DIRECT_CLOSURE_STABLE_SELECTION, DIRECT_CLOSURE_CONTEXT_OWNED_TARGET, DIRECT_CLOSURE_DIRECT_CALL_NODE, DEFINITION_KEYED_SECOND_TIER, CALL_SHADOWING_PRESERVED, GENERIC_FALLBACK_PRESERVED, OBSERVABLE_PROTOS_SEMANTIC_CHANGE=NO, FINAL_REQUIRED_VALIDATION=PASS) is already complete and is not re-validated by this Evidence Unit - see runner/perf014_direct_closure_call.py's module docstring. This config intentionally cites no specific guillermomolina/protos-project-docs commit: it is implemented from project information supplied directly to the harness author rather than from reading that repository.
causal_question: How much does the final PERF014 direct Closure-call implementation reduce the steady-state cost of a guest Closure call, once the workload-control's own measured movement between the two product revisions has been subtracted out? PERF014's structural validation passing does not by itself establish how much of the guest-call cost was actually recovered - this Evidence Unit is the causal-attribution owner for that question. The predeclared PERF014 prediction is that the closure-call-minus-workload-control guest-call increment falls by a clearly multiplicative factor once the intervention is in place; this harness retains the numbers needed to evaluate that prediction (see guest_call_increment_formula) but deliberately does not itself decide whether "clearly multiplicative" is satisfied - see timing_classification_note.

control.protos_revision_note: PERF013 B2, the exact baseline this Evidence Unit compares the final PERF014 product against. Built as an ordinary VARIANT=baseline image (no patch is applied to either PERF014 image - see both_variants_baseline/patches_applied below).

intervention.protos_revision_note: The final published PERF014 product revision (guillermomolina/protos#725). Built as an ordinary VARIANT=baseline image from its own checkout; the Protos revision is the only intended difference in code between the two images. See intervening_unrelated_revision below - the intervention is not related to the control by PERF014 commits alone, which is why workload_identity_policy's read-back check is required rather than assumed from lineage.

intervening_unrelated_revision.note: BUG010, an intervening commit in the intervention's ancestry between the control and the final PERF014 product that does NOT belong to PERF014. BUG010 touches only Test Tool/reporting surfaces and metadata (CHANGELOG.md, pom.xml, protos/tools/test/LogicalCaseRunner.protos, protos/tools/test/Main.protos, Test Tool Java tests); it does not modify ProtosBytecodeRootNode or any benchmark workload source. Recorded here for lineage honesty only: control and intervention are therefore NOT described as a direct PERF014-only parent/child pair. This note does NOT relax or replace the exact revision/version identity checks in validate()/smoke()/reference(), nor the workload_identity_policy read-back check below - both still run unconditionally.

patches_applied_note: This comparator never builds a VARIANT=ablation image and never supplies a non-empty ablation_patch for either role; docker/protos-perf010a/Dockerfile only applies a patch when VARIANT=ablation, so both the control and intervention images are ordinary, unmodified baseline builds of their own pinned protos_revision. The harness additionally reads back each built image's /opt/perf010a/ablation-slice.txt (must be exactly 'none' for both roles) before any timing runs.

historical_evidence.perf014_first_tier_context_only_not_used: cc76159a1bc9e2e1d46363f1c9047aa1034474df (0.3.103-SNAPSHOT) - the first PERF014 implementation, keyed only by exact receiver identity; superseded by the definition-keyed second tier under comparison here and not itself a role in this Evidence Unit

jfr_recording_note: Clean causal timing only - no JFR, no TraceCompilation/compiler tracing, no IGV, no allocation profiling, no diagnosticSampling, no Test Tool diagnostics, no source-identity instrumentation - see AGENTS.work/REPRODUCIBILITY.md's diagnostic-instrumentation/timing separation rule. Reuses the exact steady-state-only timing discipline already accepted by config/perf010a-post-i072-fprime.json and config/perf010a-phase2.json.
cpu_affinity: one physical-core representative from current allowed cpuset
workload_coverage_note: PERF014 changes only the direct Closure-call path (ProtosClosureValue invocation), so micro/closure-call is the sole PRIMARY causal workload for this Evidence Unit's causal_question. micro/slot-read, micro/method-call and runtime/monomorphic-dispatch do not exercise a Closure call site and are retained as broader negative coverage - they discriminate a real closure-call-specific effect from generic whole-runtime movement between the two product revisions. The retained full Evidence Unit still includes all four workloads unconditionally. The closure-call result MUST NOT be generalized to method-call/monomorphic-dispatch/slot-read or to any whole-language performance claim.
workload_identity_policy: Both product revisions must execute materially identical benchmark programs. Before any timing, the harness reads back each workload's exact canonical source text (/opt/perf010a/corpus/<source>) from both the built control and intervention images and fails closed (WORKLOAD_SOURCE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH) if their SHA-256 digests differ for any workload in `controls`, rather than silently comparing a changed program across revisions. This check is especially load-bearing for this Evidence Unit because, per intervening_unrelated_revision above, the intervention is not related to the control by PERF014 commits alone - control and intervention are two real published product revisions, not a minimal single-commit diff. See workload_source_sha256 in the retained raw.json for the digests actually observed by the reference run.
block_order_note: Deterministic AB/BA counterbalanced design, 4 blocks (2 reps of each order), no randomness - reuses the exact counterbalancing discipline already accepted by config/perf010a-post-i072-fprime.json and config/perf010a-phase2.json. Block 'A': CONTROL runs first, INTERVENTION second. Block 'B': INTERVENTION runs first, CONTROL second. Canonical/workload-control pairing within a revision/role is preserved in both orders; only which revision/role runs first is counterbalanced.
causal_formula: canonical_improvement = control_canonical_median_ns - intervention_canonical_median_ns; control_movement = control_workload_control_median_ns - intervention_workload_control_median_ns; paired_control_effect = canonical_improvement - control_movement. A positive paired_control_effect means INTERVENTION is faster than CONTROL once the workload-control's own measured movement between the two revisions/images has been subtracted out. Reused unchanged from config/perf010a-post-i072-fprime.json's causal_formula.
guest_call_increment_formula: PERF014-specific, micro/closure-call only, additional to and never a replacement for causal_formula's paired_control_effect. Per block: CONTROL_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT = control_canonical_median_ns - control_workload_control_median_ns; INTERVENTION_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT = intervention_canonical_median_ns - intervention_workload_control_median_ns; GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT_REDUCTION = CONTROL_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT - INTERVENTION_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT. GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT_RATIO = CONTROL_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT / INTERVENTION_GUEST_CALL_INCREMENT only when both increments are strictly positive, else NOT_APPLICABLE. The retained Evidence Unit reports this both per block (so ratio/reduction stability can be inspected across the 4 blocks rather than trusted from a single aggregate quotient) and as an aggregate (median of the 4 per-block increments, with the ratio taken from the two aggregate medians).
not_decided_by_this_evidence_unit: whether the guest-call increment reduction is "clearly multiplicative" (PERF014_CLEARLY_MULTIPLICATIVE)
any whole-language performance claim ("Protos is Nx faster/slower") from these microbenchmarks
selection or scoping of any further production optimization
timing_classification_note: This Evidence Unit deliberately does not classify PERF014_TIMING_CLASSIFICATION, PERF014_CLEARLY_MULTIPLICATIVE, or PERF015_AUTHORIZED from its own retained data: `reference` prints and retains the raw computed per-workload paired_control_effect statistics and the guest_call_increment_summary (median/MAD/min/max, per-block series, order effect) but leaves those three fields as explicit NOT_CLASSIFIED/NOT_CLASSIFIED/NO placeholders in raw.json and README.md. No threshold (e.g. exactly 2x, 5x, 10x) is hardcoded anywhere in this harness for that decision. The classification is a later interpretation step performed by a human or a subsequent investigation slice reading this Evidence Unit's raw retained data, not part of this harness - matching config/perf010a-post-i072-fprime.json's identical scale_classification_note discipline for its own analogous unclassified fields.
